newsitem.title: USA: NYC Republicans say not-for-profits waste money.
newsitem.headline: NYC Republicans say not-for-profits waste money.

text.p: New York City Council Republicans Tuesday unveiled a report saying almost one-third of not-for-profit agencies the city hired overpaid their executives, and submitted a bill giving them more oversight.

The city allocates one-tenth of the tax dollars it collects to not-for-profit organizations, about the same sum that the police department gets to fight crime, according to Council Member Vito Fosello. Such groups include childrens' societies and ones that assist the needy, for example.

Fifty-six of the not-for-profits have contracts with one or more of four city agencies, the Human Resources Administration, the Department of Social Servicees, the Department of Mental Health, and the Department of Aging.
About 29 percent of the groups surveyed in 1994 paid their executive directors more than the typical city commissioner, who earned $110,000, the report said.

Top officials at New York City's smaller charitable organizations earned much more than their counterparts throughout the nation. Outfits with less than $5 million in functional expenses paid their executive directors a median salary of $70,422. This was 51 percent more than the national median of $46,535 paid by groups of about the same size.
The report also found big differences in the salaries paid by not-for-profits that had about the same size budget.

The biggest not-for-profits had the fattest executive salaries, which ranged from $79,750 to $245,802 among those whose functional expenses were over $25 million. But the smallest outfits, those with less than $5 million of functional expenses, also could be generous: their directors received from $28,284 to $169,395.

"A tax dollar going to a city agency gets reviewed, analyzed and evaluted. A tax dollar going to a not-for-profit gets a 'see ya later, hope you end up at your proper destination'," said City Council Minority Whip John Fusco, in prepared remarks.

The Council Republicans also faulted the not-for-profit agencies for failing to provide complete information. The three Republican members said their bill would give the council "an active oversight role" over not-for-profits that got contracts with the city that were worth $100,000 or more.

"Unfortunately, as not-for-profits have grown into a multi-billion dollar industry, the oversight by city government of these organizations continues to be essentially non-existent," said Council Republican Leader Thomas Ognibene.
